subject: art-design
title: Annotation & Analysis: Application
welcome_lead: Use a structured method — description, analysis, interpretation, judgement.
meta_desc: Applying the Feldman model of analysis at GCSE: describe, analyse, interpret, judge.
final_note: A method stops you from drifting into vague comments.

concepts.def: Saying what is literally visible in the work.
How formal elements are organised together.
An evidenced opinion on success of the piece.
When, where and why the work was made.
Based on personal feeling rather than fact.

walkthroughs.body_html: Write only what is visible: size, materials, subject, colours. Avoid words like "beautiful" yet — they belong in judgement. A clear description stops you talking about a piece you have not actually looked at.
How is the composition arranged? Where is the focal point? What contrast between light and dark? What palette and why? Analysis shows how the artist's choices push the viewer's eye through the work.

Interpretation suggests meaning — supported by what you have just analysed. Judgement gives an opinion backed by reasons, comparing to context: was the piece original for its time, does it succeed in its goal?

options: Dark colours always advance.

Cool colours like blue.
Just measurements.

mcqs.q: What are the three primary colours in paint (subtractive)?
options: Cool colours like blue.
Black, white, and grey.
Red, green, and blue.
Red, yellow, and blue (or magenta, yellow, cyan in print).
